- If sentiment turns sharply bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overreact and overshoot; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume drops to 0, model often underreacts; increase forecast by 1–2% to counteract mean reversion.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume is high (≥3), model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment momentum.
- If model forecast spikes >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection; especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over 5+ days, model often underestimates upside; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and news volume is low (≤2), model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near the end of the forecast window; reduce final 3–5 days by 0.5–1.5% to reflect diminishing momentum.
